note: ONE shared expectation for two resolvers that cannot call each other. The macOS shell (Sources/HasnaConversationsCore) decides which store the bundled server will use and then builds the environment it hands that server; src/lib/store/index.ts is what the server actually resolves with. They diverged: the shell read 3 env vars, the resolver honours 8, and 5 of the uncovered ones select the local store — so the shell logged store=hosted while the child served local SQLite, silently. Each arm below carries the input, what the shell must announce, and the exact store-selecting keys the child must receive. Tests/HasnaConversationsCoreTests asserts the shell half; src/lib/store/store-resolution-matrix.test.ts asserts the TypeScript resolver reaches the same store from that child environment. Neither half can drift without the other's test failing.

arms.name: arm1-prefixed-url-and-key
arms.note: The fleet flip signal. Correct before and after the fix.

arms.name: arm2-inherited-prefixed-db-path-outranks-url-and-key
arms.note: BEFORE: shell announced hosted, child resolved local. NOW: no config file is present, so the inherited environment is all there is, and DB_PATH is the resolver's highest-precedence signal — the shell announces local and the child gets local. Announcement matches outcome.

arms.name: arm3-inherited-unprefixed-db-path-outranks-url-and-key
arms.note: Same as arm2 through the unprefixed alias, which the old shell could not see at all.

arms.name: arm4-inherited-unprefixed-mode-local
arms.note: CONVERSATIONS_MODE is one of the four mode keys the resolver honours and the old shell read none of the last three.

arms.name: arm5-inherited-prefixed-alias-mode-local
arms.note: HASNA_CONVERSATIONS_MODE, the near-miss alias of the one key the old shell did read.

arms.name: arm6-unprefixed-url-and-key-only
arms.note: The mirror-image failure: the old shell saw neither key and refused to start on a configuration the resolver accepts. Failing closed, so an availability bug rather than a correctness one — now resolved and re-emitted under the canonical names.

arms.name: arm2f-fleet-config-beats-inherited-prefixed-db-path
arms.note: THE DEPLOYED SHAPE, and the one the owner is waiting on. The fleet config file names the hosted service; a stray inherited DB_PATH must not silently redirect the app to a different dataset. The file outranks the inherited environment and the DB_PATH never reaches the child.

arms.name: file-explicit-local-is-honoured
arms.note: Local is fully supported when it is asked for by name — the guard refuses ambiguity, not local storage.

arms.name: file-deprecated-alias-self-hosted-is-cloud
arms.note: normalizeStorageMode maps remote/hybrid/self_hosted to cloud. The shell carries the operator's token through unchanged rather than inventing one.

arms.name: key-without-url-uses-the-default-host
arms.note: The transport defaults the base URL when a key is present and no URL is set. The shell must announce that same default rather than refuse a configuration the resolver accepts.

arms.name: file-url-without-key-refuses
arms.note: Half a cloud configuration is an error, never a fall-back to local. The reviewer listed this branch as having no evidence behind it.

arms.name: unrecognised-mode-refuses
arms.note: The resolver throws on an unknown token rather than guessing; the shell must not guess either.

arms.name: non-http-url-refuses
arms.note: assertUsableApiUrl refuses a URL the transport could not use. Mirrored here so the shell does not start a server that will throw.

arms.name: nothing-configured-fails-closed
arms.note: The one deliberate divergence from the TypeScript resolver, and the reason this app exists: with nothing configured the library documents local SQLite as the single-operator default, while the app refuses to start. No child is launched, so the two cannot disagree about a running server. This is the exact string measured on station06 as arm B of the fail-closed pair.
